summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and recent coronary stenting presented with an episode of shortness of breath and substernal chest pressure that occurred at home after a dialysis session. The symptoms resolved with aspirin and oxygen in the ambulance. Evaluation showed stable cardiac enzymes and an unchanged EKG, with no evidence of acute coronary syndrome. The clinical picture was consistent with symptoms related to post-dialysis fluid shifts rather than a new cardiac event. The patient remained stable throughout the brief admission, continued on his baseline cardiac and renal medications, and was discharged home with instructions to follow up with his cardiologist and nephrologist.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
